paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption: : Coverage.
model_annotation:
This plot illustrates the coverage metric as a function of the number of completions for four model variants. The x-axis represents the number of completions (*k*), displayed on a logarithmic (base-2) scale ranging from 2⁰ (1) to 2⁸ (256), with tick labels at each power of two. The y-axis represents coverage on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 0.4 to 0.9, with gridlines visible at 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and approximately 0.9.

Four lines are shown. The dark blue line with filled circle markers represents "Llama-3B," starting at approximately 0.43 at *k* = 1 and increasing steadily to approximately 0.90 at *k* = 256. The green dashed line with filled square markers represents "Llama-3B + FT," starting at approximately 0.50 at *k* = 1 and rising to approximately 0.88 at *k* = 256, tracking closely with the Llama-3B line at higher *k* values but starting notably higher. The light blue line with open circle markers represents "Llama-1B," starting at approximately 0.42 at *k* = 1 and increasing to approximately 0.87 at *k* = 256. The light green line with open triangle markers represents "Llama-1B + FT," starting at approximately 0.48 at *k* = 1 and rising to approximately 0.86 at *k* = 256. All four lines exhibit monotonically increasing trends that begin to plateau at higher values of *k*, with the fine-tuned (+ FT) variants of both model sizes showing higher coverage at low *k* values compared to their non-fine-tuned counterparts, while the lines converge at higher *k* values.
